summary: Mesh routing flap in edge fabric causing extended TLS handshake and request timeouts for us-west customers
description:
Issue summary:
Customers in the us-west region are observing elevated request latencies and sporadic request timeouts. The symptoms trace to an edge mesh routing flap that produces prolonged TLS handshake duration and occasional connection resets when the gateway picks a cross-region egress path.

Impact:
- Multiple Clipstitch Media endpoints experienced 5-10% request failures (timeouts) during the window; p95 increased from ~120ms to ~2.1s for text generation calls.
- Affected features: streaming responses sometimes disconnect mid-stream; non-streaming generation requests hit 504s after backend timeout.

Environment:
- Prod customers in us-west region on Dedicated pools
- API endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/stream
- Proxy layer: edge-nginx mesh with smart-routing enabled

Observed behavior:
1) Client establishes TCP but TLS handshake time increases unpredictably (handshake durations sampling at 800ms-1.8s).
2) When handshake times exceed backend connect timeout, gateway returns 504 or terminates stream.
3) Traces show egress chosen intermittently to eu-west peering path instead of local direct egress; that path has known higher RTT and transient packet reordering.

Expected behavior:
- Edge mesh should prefer local direct egress to minimize handshake latency and should not select cross-region egress for low-latency traffic unless local path is degraded per policy.

Steps to reproduce:
1) From a us-west client simulate 1000 rapid generation requests to /v1/generate with default timeouts.
2) Observe p95/p99 and TLS handshake metrics on the request traces.
3) Re-run while toggling smart-routing policy to force-local vs default to see delta.

Additional notes:
- Customer provided request IDs and timestamps in logs below.
- Issue appears correlated with a mesh control-plane event at approx 2026-03-10T02:14:00Z (control-plane roll for route weights).

comments: Support - Lina Park (2026-03-10): Customer reports intermittent timeouts and streaming disconnects. Initial triage suggests TLS handshake spikes. Pinging SRE for routing context (#support).

SRE - Mateo Alvarez (2026-03-10): Correlated anomaly in control-plane route weights at 2026-03-10T02:14:00Z. Some nodes temporarily selected eastus peer egress for us-west traffic. Gathering node-level logs and eBPF flow captures.
Customer - Sarah Kim (Clipstitch) (2026-03-10): Saw 504s around 02:14-02:20Z, replays attached. This impacts nightly thumbnail generation jobs.

SRE - Mateo Alvarez (2026-03-11): Deployed hotfix to the control-plane weighting algorithm to prevent aggressive rebalancing. For immediate mitigation we forced local-egress policy for Clipstitch's dedicated pool. Monitoring metrics for 12 hours.
Support - Lina Park (2026-03-12): Customer confirmed reduced timeouts after forced local-egress, but asked for root cause and permanent fix. Escalating to infra-owner for post-mortem.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: control-plane route weight update caused transient misclassification of local egress health, resulting in selection of higher-latency peering path.
Node logs show control-plane push at 02:14:00Z with delta weights for edge-nginx group 7; several nodes accepted new policy but their health-checks for local egress were stale (healthcache TTL=30s).
eBPF captures show packet reordering and increased retransmits on peer path, amplifying TLS handshake duration due to packet loss/reordering sensitivity in TLS record layer.
Observed that the failover policy allows cross-region egress if local-egress healthcheck has not been refreshed; race between weight update and healthcheck refresh causes incorrect fallback.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: 1) Forced local-egress routing for Clipstitch dedicated pool; 2) Rolled back aggressive weight delta in control-plane; 3) Increased healthcheck refresh frequency for egress interfaces from 30s -> 5s and added a short hysteresis window to prevent immediate cross-region selection. Work in progress: infra team to land permanent fix in control-plane service and add automated canary for route change impact. Customer notified and monitoring shows p95 halved after mitigation.
next_steps: Infra to merge PR to control-plane to add canary checks and healthcache invalidation (PR referenced above).
Create a runbook entry for routing-change rollback and include step to force local-egress for Dedicated pools as emergency mitigation.
Postmortem to be authored and linked here once complete.
